To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the myosin SRX state is a new state of myofibrillar myosin that is characterized by a low rate of ATP hydrolysis and that is inhibited by binding to the thick filament, and 2) the SRX state is an important contributor to adaptive thermogenic responses of muscle to exposure to cold and to overfeeding, and that modulation of its population by pharmaceuticals may provide a new approach to the treatment of metabolic disorders.

myosin is a key player in thermogenesis by skeletal muscles, that the myosin SRX is a key component in thermogenesis, and that the myosine regulatory light chain is a target for pharmaceuticals that can be used for the treatment of obesity and diabetes.

a new state of myofibrillar myosin, with a very slow turnover rate, has been identified in skeletal muscle, and that modulation of the fraction of myosin in this state is proposed to be a key factor in adaptive thermogenesis in skeletal muscle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanism that underlies adaptive thermogenesis by resting muscle.
understanding how the SRX is formed and regulated.
the role of myosin in adaptive thermogenesis and the identification of new pharmaceuticals to modulate this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the myosin SRX is a potential target for drugs to treat obesity and high blood sugar levels.
the SRX of myosin is a major contributor, perhaps the major contributor, to adaptive thermogenesis by resting skeletal muscle.
the myosin SRX state is the furnace of muscle thermogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the myosin heads in the SRX may be the “furnaces” that generate the extra heat in adaptive thermogenesis.
the ATPase activity of myosin in skeletal muscle plays a key role in adaptive thermogenesis.
we have shown the existence of a new state of myofilaments, the super relaxed filament state (SRFS), that is a major contributor for thermogenesis in skeletal muscle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
myosin is a major contributor, and perhaps the main contributor, to adaptive thermogenesis by resting skeletal muscle.
the myosin heads in the super relaxed state are the “furnaces” that generate heat in resting muscle.
the SRX of skeletal muscle myosin may be an important contributor to the adaptive thermogenesis of resting skeletal muscle.
